component.name: Apache HertzBeat
component.description: Real-time monitoring system. HertzBeat is highly extensible: users can add custom monitoring templates (SQL, SHELL, JMX, URL, and API scripts), custom code plugins that run in the system life cycle, custom collectors, and custom URL/parameter configuration. The security model draws the boundary at these extension points: extension content is the responsibility of the authorized users who supply it.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

threats.name: Unauthorized access via unchanged default account credentials
threats.description: HertzBeat ships default account credentials. The security model instructs organizations to modify the default account credentials immediately upon deployment; a deployment that keeps them is exposed to unauthorized access.

threats.name: All users hold management privileges while RBAC is under development
threats.description: User access control is provided through the Sureness framework, but role-based access control functionality remains under development; currently all users possess management privileges. Any authenticated user therefore has full management capability over the system.

threats.name: Malicious content in custom monitoring templates
threats.description: Users can define monitoring rules through custom templates incorporating SQL, SHELL, JMX, URL, and API scripts. Template creators bear sole responsibility for content security: content must not contain malicious code or unsafe elements, and organizations should review templates before deployment. Malicious template content is the template author's responsibility, not a HertzBeat vulnerability.

threats.name: Malicious or unsafe custom code plugins
threats.description: HertzBeat supports uploading custom code plugins that run in the life cycle of multiple systems. Users need to ensure the security of the custom plugin code themselves; plugin developers assume complete security liability for uploaded code.

threats.name: Malicious or unsafe custom collectors
threats.description: Users may develop custom collectors to personalize metrics collection. As with plugins, developers must independently validate collector security prior to deployment; collector code security is the developer's responsibility.

threats.name: Abuse of custom URL and parameter configuration by authorized users
threats.description: The system permits custom URL and other parameter configuration. All users authorized to configure URLs and other parameters are considered highly trusted and are expected to trigger certain behaviors; abuse by such users is outside the model. All extension capabilities operate within authenticated user boundaries.

controls.name: Change default account credentials on deployment
controls.description: Modify the default account credentials immediately upon deployment, following the Account Permission Management guide.

controls.name: Configure user accounts, roles, and API permissions in sureness.yml
controls.description: HertzBeat uses the Sureness framework for user access control. Organizations should implement the sureness.yml configuration to establish user accounts, roles, and API resource permissions, noting that role-based access control functionality remains under development and currently all users possess management privileges.

controls.name: Review monitoring templates before deployment
controls.description: Organizations should implement review processes before deploying custom monitoring templates; template content must not contain malicious code or unsafe elements.

controls.name: Assess the security of custom plugins, collectors, and other customizations
controls.description: Developers must ensure the security of custom plugin and collector code themselves, and organizations should conduct security assessments for custom implementations across the platform ecosystem.
